title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E04 — The Problem of Pseudonymity
This lecture considers the broad problem of pseudonymity, or forgery, in the ancient world; applying one's findings to the Pauline letters of the New Testament to see if any, in fact, are written by Paul's followers rather than Paul himself.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E01 — The Historical Study of Christianity
The historical trajectory of Christianity; contemporary ignorance of its past; considering the value of the historical study of Christianity; looking at the methods and role of the historian; the sources and limitations of historical knowledge.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E02 — The First Cultural Context - Greece and Rome
Investigating the culture of the Mediterranean world in which Christianity is born; the legacy of Alexander; the features of Greek politics, religion and philosophy; learning about the nature of Roman rule and imperial order in the region.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E03 — The First Cultural Context - Judaism
The circumstances of Jewish life in ancient Palestine and the diaspora; examining cultural and ideological factors that divide the Jews; the tensions they face between assimilation and separation; their resistance to Greek culture and Roman rule.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E04 — The Jesus Movement and the Birth of Christianity
Considering the resurrection as marking the birth of Christianity, as rooted in the claims of the first believers; assessing the contradiction between Jesus as the source of divine life and the degrading manner of his death.

title: How Jesus Became God
description:
S01 E01 — Jesus - The Man Who Became God
The historical significance of the Christian belief in Jesus's divinity, in terms of its effects on Western civilization; learning about different scholarly views of the historical Jesus; tracing the diversity of early Christian thought.

title: How Jesus Became God
description:
S01 E02 — Greco-Roman Gods Who Became Human
The accounts of divine mortals in the ancient world; the overlap between the human and divine worlds in Greco-Roman polytheistic religions; exploring three age-old models of divine men in both mythology and Christian scripture.

title: How Jesus Became God
description:
S01 E03 — Humans as Gods in the Greco-Roman World
Delving into the interface between the human and the divine in pagan cultures; examining narratives describing people born of the sexual union of gods with mortals; looking at cases of humans who were exalted to the status of gods.

title: How Jesus Became God
description:
S01 E04 — Gods Who Were Human in Ancient Judaism
Accounts of divine humans and other godlike beings within ancient Judaism; exploring conceptions of divine beings that appear in human form in Genesis and Exodus; studying narratives of humans who become angelic beings in other Jewish texts.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E01 — The Birth of Christianity
This lecture introduces some issues essential to understanding how Christianity begins; growing away from its Jewish roots; ultimately becoming the most important religion of the civilization.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E02 — The Religious World of Early Christianity
This lecture introduces the pagan, polytheistic religions that dominate the early world; the most important Roman religion for the birth of Christianity; Judaism, the religion of Jesus and his followers.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E03 — The Historical Jesus
In the first of three lectures on the birth of Christianity, Professor Ehrman examines the life of Jesus of Nazareth; referred to both outside the New Testament and within the Gospels themselves.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E04 — Oral and Written Traditions about Jesus
How four anonymous authors who live decades after Jesus record traditions that have been circulating orally over the intervening years; examining the extent to which those traditions have been modified in the retelling.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E01 — The New Testament-An Overview
The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E02 — Paul-Our Earliest Christian Author
The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E03 — The Pauline Epistles
This lecture looks at some of the major teachings of Paul's Epistles; showing how he shapes his theological and ethical views in light of the problems that emerge in his burgeoning Christian communities.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E01 — Your Ancestry, Your Identity
Asking whether genes determine one's essential nature and identity, or one builds their own identity; exploring the essentialist and constructed philosophies; how one might incorporate aspects of both into their own view of personal identity.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E02 — What Genetic Testing Brings to Ancestry
Labs that provide DNA ancestry information use hundreds of thousands of ancestry-information markers, or AIMs; learning about the AIMs that relate to major identifiable lineages; what can be gleaned from mitochondrial DNA and Y-DNA.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E03 — Sensitive Approaches to Ancestry Results
There are many social issues affecting an individual's emotional response to receiving DNA ancestry results; how the reciprocal engagement method can help families face unexpected ancestry results; tips to consider before ordering one's own test.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E04 — When Family Narrative Meets Genetic Testing
People want a family narrative, whereas DNA just "wants" to move itself forward and is neutral on issues of race, subterfuge or social connection; how to create a strategic family narrative to incorporate the scientific facts of DNA ancestry results.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E05 — Privacy Versus Connection in DNA Testing
From the case of Henrietta Lacks to that of the Hagahai people of Papua New Guinea, scientists and government agencies have a history of bad actions with respect to biological samples; learn about the laws and programs in place to protect privacy.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E06 — The DNA Discussion Project Research
Learning about the DNA Discussion Project and its goals; current results regarding the ways in which DNA ancestry tests are changing identity; looking at questions about unanticipated results, sharing DNA ancestry results and social implications.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E07 — How Genograms Reveal Your Ancestry
A genogram is a graphic tool used to explore family history and relationships over a two- to three-generation period, discovering the powerful information that can be conveyed through a genogram as opposed to the traditional family tree diagram.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E08 — Gaining Insight Through Your Genetics
Exploring the issue of birth assisted by reproductive technologies by meeting Maria, who learns as a teenager that she was born with the help of intrauterine insemination; considering how this knowledge affects an adolescent's identity.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E01 — Greeks and Macedonians
Philip II of Macedon sets the stage for the rise of his son, Alexander the Great, by conquering Greece; when Alexander invades the Persian territory of Asia Minor in 334 B.C., he embarks on the greatest career of conquest the world has ever seen.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E02 — Alexander the Divine?
After only two battles, Alexander commands more land than any Greek before him; he orders the Persian emperor to address him as an equal; at the height of his power, he visits Egypt, where he assumes the title of pharaoh and is hailed as a deity.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E03 — The Blazing Star
Whether his Egyptian sojourn convinces Alexander that he is a god or just teaches him the political value of blurring the lines between human and divine; how Alexander brings the Persian emperor to battle as he resumes his drive eastward.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E04 — Alexander-Myth and Reality
Alexander has an effect on the political development of the eastern Mediterranean; opinions about him remain deeply divided, both in antiquity and the current day; whether one can discern the historical Alexander, or the myth has swallowed the man.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E05 — The Formation of the Kingdoms
A generation of warfare among Alexander's successors splits his empire; after these "wars of the Diadochi", three major Hellenistic kingdoms emerge under the control of Alexander's former officers.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E06 — Egypt Under the Early Ptolemies
Ptolemy, one of Alexander's companions, transforms himself into a new pharaoh in Egypt even as he remains separate from the conquered Egyptians; how Ptolemy and his successors blend Pharaonic and Macedonian practices to create a new kingdom.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E07 — Alexandria and the Library
Alexandria is the seat of Ptolemy's court; the city's library and museum are the premier cultural institutions of the Hellenistic world; and whether Alexandria is a blend of Greek and Egyptian elements or the imposition of one culture over the other.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E08 — The Seleucid Realm
The second great Hellenistic kingdom is ruled by the Seleucid dynasty, which builds cities from Syria to Iran, learning how the Seleucids rule a kingdom that stretches across all of Central Asia.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E05 — How Do Archaeologists Know Where to Dig?
The methods archeologists use in looking for sites; the uses of remote sensing technologies, which enable archeologists to visualize objects obscured by vegetation and soil; investigating ground surveys, which reveal information before digging.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E06 — Prehistoric Archaeology
Prehistoric archeology allows one to glimpse the earliest times in hominid and human history; learning about seminal 20th-century finds of hominids in Africa; discovering the figural cave paintings of Lascaux, Altamira and Chauvet.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E07 — Göbekli Tepe, Çatalhöyük, and Jericho
Significant Neolithic sites; exploring Gobekli Tepe, whose stone rings are the oldest known examples of monumental architecture in the early Near East; the tombs and tower of Jericho; Catalhoyuk is noted for its houses without doors or windows.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E08 — Pyramids, Mummies, and Hieroglyphics
A first look at the wonders of Egyptology; the deciphering of hieroglyphics; the techniques of ancient Egyptian embalming and mummification; the stories behind the building of the Step Pyramid of Zozer, the Pyramids at Giza and the Sphinx.

title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
description:
S01 E05 — Alexander the Great: Greek Culture Spreads
The conquests of Alexander the Great give birth to the Hellenistic world; Alexander's military expansionism brings a vast geographical area under the Greek civilization; Alexander's empire fragments after his death; Alexandria, a center of learning.

title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
description:
S01 E06 — Greece, Rome, Byzantium, and Baghdad
The conflicted relationship between the Greeks and their Roman conquerors; Greek culture's impact on Rome; the founding of the Byzantine Empire, its flourishing of scholarship and theology; the role of Islamic scholars in preserving Greek learning.

title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
description:
S01 E07 — Modern Ideas of Ancient Greece
Constantinople's fall in 1453; the Greeks under the Ottomans; Europe rediscovers classical antiquity; the philosophical spirit of the Renaissance, which brings a sudden interest in the ancient Greeks; the influence of Greek mythology on Western art.

title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
description:
S01 E08 — The Birth of the Greek Nation-State
The struggle of the Greeks under the Ottomans; European intellectuals and Europe's major powers support the movement to free Greece; the nation-state of Greece in 1830; Greece's territorial expansion; its tumultuous modern history up to the present.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E05 — Platonism and Stoicism
The influence of philosophy on the morality and conduct of Rome's ruling classes; an influence rarely matched in the Western tradition; Christian theologians employing the doctrines of these two philosophical schools in defining their own faith.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E06 — Jews in the Roman Empire
Knowing what role Judaism plays in the Roman Empire; learning how Rome's experience with this stalwart monotheistic faith, the first it has encountered, differs from the challenge of the Christian faith that emerges from it.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E07 — Christian Challenge - First Conversions
The first years of efforts to convert people to Christianity; the early leadership by James of those who are often called Jewish Christians; the career of Paul, from his own conversion after a vision to his work propagating the message of Jesus.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E08 — Pagan Response - First Persecutions
Early responses to Christianity; the violent persecutions in Rome under Nero; the legalistic and easily avoided persecutions under later emperors; Roman ignorance of Christianity; the eventual momentum that ignorance gives the new faith.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E05 — Origins of Greek Civilization
As the Hittites unite Anatolia, early Greeks called Achaeans visit its western reaches; Achaean warlords trade and raid along the shores of Asia Minor; in time, they become the first Greeks to clash with the armies of a great king to the east.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E06 — The Legend of Troy
The most enduring legacies from early Anatolia are "The Iliad" and "The Odyssey": how the siege of Troy and the exploits of Homer's warrior chieftains fit into the wider tale of imperial struggle and decline during the Greek Dark Age.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E07 — Iron Age Kingdoms of Asia Minor
From 1200 B.C. to 1000 B.C., migrations reshape Anatolia; Phrygians come from the Balkans, only to be overcome by Cimmerian nomads; in the West, Hittite provincials found trade-rich Lydia, whose last king is Croesus.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E08 — Emergence of the Polis
From 750 B.C., the Greeks distinguish themselves with the polis, a city-state based on citizen rule; by 500 B.C., Athens devises the first democratic constitution, with all adult male citizens forming the sovereign assembly.

title: Reconsidering JFK
description:
S01 E01 — JFK Reconsidered
Discovering how JFK excels at compartmentalizing his life so that few, if anyone, truly knows him.

title: Reconsidering JFK
description:
S01 E02 — 1956: Vice President Kennedy?
Exploring the backroom deals of a party that expects the young politician to pay his dues.

title: Reconsidering JFK
description:
S01 E03 — JFK's Pivotal Choices to Win the Presidency
Surveying JFK's campaign against the seasoned politician Richard Nixon.

title: Reconsidering JFK
description:
S01 E04 — Unearthing JFK's Public and Private Lives
JFK is a well-known playboy, something of an open secret in Washington during his time in office.

title: Liberty on Trial in America: Cases That Defined Freedom
description:
S01 E01 — The Trial of Anne Hutchinson
There is no toleration of religious dissent in the Massachusetts Bay Colony in the 1600s; Anne Hutchinson shares with others her religious ideas and gathers a following; the governor puts her on trial for heresy; the trials and punishment of Anne.

title: Liberty on Trial in America: Cases That Defined Freedom
description:
S01 E02 — The Trial of John Peter Zenger
Freedom of speech is not recognized liberty; speech critical of the powers can land one in legal trouble; the colonial history of press freedom; attempts to influence juries as they try to affect the libel trial of John Peter Zenger.

title: Liberty on Trial in America: Cases That Defined Freedom
description:
S01 E03 — Two Slave Trials
The citizens of the newly formed United States cannot agree on the moral issue of slavery; they are willing to take up its more narrow legal issues; how the legal system supports the institution of slavery; the trials of Anthony Burns and Celia.

title: Liberty on Trial in America: Cases That Defined Freedom
description:
S01 E04 — The Trial of John Brown
John Brown's plan to end slavery comes to a tragic end at Harper's Ferry, Va.; Brown is charged with treason, murder and slave insurrection; John Brown's trial and execution play a significant role in the eventual end of slavery in the US.

title: Turning Points in American History
description:
S01 E01 — 1617 The Great Epidemic
The North American continent is never the same after the Great Epidemic of 1617; it wipes out nearly 90 percent of Native Americans and allows British colonization to proceed virtually unchallenged; the defining characteristics of a turning point.

title: Turning Points in American History
description:
S01 E02 — 1619 Land of the Free? Slavery Begins
How and why does a democratic America become a slaveholding society; exploring this paradox from its origins in 1619; slaves arrive at Jamestown; the influence of Bacon's Rebellion in 1676; the expansion of slavery throughout the South in the 1800s.

title: Turning Points in American History
description:
S01 E03 — 1636 Freedom of Worship - Roger Williams
Roger Williams's efforts to establish freedom of religion, a somewhat forgotten story from early colonial America; religious life in the early Massachusetts settlements; Williams's controversial ideas; his influence on religious freedom in America.

title: Turning Points in American History
description:
S01 E04 — 1654 Yearning to Breathe Free - Immigration
A symbolic expression of the idea that all are welcome in America takes place in 1654; the Dutch West India Company allows Jews from Brazil to settle in New Amsterdam; a gateway to understanding immigration as a central theme in American history.

title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
description:
S01 E01 — Young Man Lincoln
Abraham Lincoln is born with little more than his natural talents; his father is more than contented with the life of a classic Jeffersonian farmer; the Lincolns move from Indiana to Illinois; Abraham strikes out on his own and never looks back.

title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
description:
S01 E02 — Whig Meteor
Lincoln's entry into politics coincides with the emergence of a new national political party, the Whigs; Lincoln at the forefront of Whig agitation to improve business; his own business ventures flop; he takes up law in Springfield, Illinois.

title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
description:
S01 E03 — Lincoln, Law, and Politics
Through his law partner, John Todd Stuart, Lincoln meets and marries Mary Todd in 1842; he wins the election to Congress in 1846, but his term is undistinguished; Lincoln returns to a life of domestic unhappiness; substantial success as an attorney.

title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
description:
S01 E04 — The Mind of Abraham Lincoln
Lincoln's folksiness is a shield he rarely lets down; many see him as an introverted, slightly aloof lawyer; he dislikes wanna-be aristocrats and is a tremendous reader; he believes in God, but not the God of any formal religion.

title: Reconsidering JFK
description:
S01 E01 — JFK Reconsidered
Discovering how JFK excels at compartmentalizing his life so that few, if anyone, truly knows him.

title: Reconsidering JFK
description:
S01 E02 — 1956: Vice President Kennedy?
Exploring the backroom deals of a party that expects the young politician to pay his dues.

title: Reconsidering JFK
description:
S01 E03 — JFK's Pivotal Choices to Win the Presidency
Surveying JFK's campaign against the seasoned politician Richard Nixon.

title: Reconsidering JFK
description:
S01 E04 — Unearthing JFK's Public and Private Lives
JFK is a well-known playboy, something of an open secret in Washington during his time in office.

title: Liberty on Trial in America: Cases That Defined Freedom
description:
S01 E01 — The Trial of Anne Hutchinson
There is no toleration of religious dissent in the Massachusetts Bay Colony in the 1600s; Anne Hutchinson shares with others her religious ideas and gathers a following; the governor puts her on trial for heresy; the trials and punishment of Anne.

title: Liberty on Trial in America: Cases That Defined Freedom
description:
S01 E02 — The Trial of John Peter Zenger
Freedom of speech is not recognized liberty; speech critical of the powers can land one in legal trouble; the colonial history of press freedom; attempts to influence juries as they try to affect the libel trial of John Peter Zenger.

title: Liberty on Trial in America: Cases That Defined Freedom
description:
S01 E03 — Two Slave Trials
The citizens of the newly formed United States cannot agree on the moral issue of slavery; they are willing to take up its more narrow legal issues; how the legal system supports the institution of slavery; the trials of Anthony Burns and Celia.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E05 — How Do Archaeologists Know Where to Dig?
The methods archeologists use in looking for sites; the uses of remote sensing technologies, which enable archeologists to visualize objects obscured by vegetation and soil; investigating ground surveys, which reveal information before digging.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E06 — Prehistoric Archaeology
Prehistoric archeology allows one to glimpse the earliest times in hominid and human history; learning about seminal 20th-century finds of hominids in Africa; discovering the figural cave paintings of Lascaux, Altamira and Chauvet.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E07 — Göbekli Tepe, Çatalhöyük, and Jericho
Significant Neolithic sites; exploring Gobekli Tepe, whose stone rings are the oldest known examples of monumental architecture in the early Near East; the tombs and tower of Jericho; Catalhoyuk is noted for its houses without doors or windows.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E08 — Pyramids, Mummies, and Hieroglyphics
A first look at the wonders of Egyptology; the deciphering of hieroglyphics; the techniques of ancient Egyptian embalming and mummification; the stories behind the building of the Step Pyramid of Zozer, the Pyramids at Giza and the Sphinx.

title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
description:
S01 E05 — Alexander the Great: Greek Culture Spreads
The conquests of Alexander the Great give birth to the Hellenistic world; Alexander's military expansionism brings a vast geographical area under the Greek civilization; Alexander's empire fragments after his death; Alexandria, a center of learning.

title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
description:
S01 E06 — Greece, Rome, Byzantium, and Baghdad
The conflicted relationship between the Greeks and their Roman conquerors; Greek culture's impact on Rome; the founding of the Byzantine Empire, its flourishing of scholarship and theology; the role of Islamic scholars in preserving Greek learning.

title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
description:
S01 E07 — Modern Ideas of Ancient Greece
Constantinople's fall in 1453; the Greeks under the Ottomans; Europe rediscovers classical antiquity; the philosophical spirit of the Renaissance, which brings a sudden interest in the ancient Greeks; the influence of Greek mythology on Western art.

title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
description:
S01 E08 — The Birth of the Greek Nation-State
The struggle of the Greeks under the Ottomans; European intellectuals and Europe's major powers support the movement to free Greece; the nation-state of Greece in 1830; Greece's territorial expansion; its tumultuous modern history up to the present.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E05 — Platonism and Stoicism
The influence of philosophy on the morality and conduct of Rome's ruling classes; an influence rarely matched in the Western tradition; Christian theologians employing the doctrines of these two philosophical schools in defining their own faith.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E06 — Jews in the Roman Empire
Knowing what role Judaism plays in the Roman Empire; learning how Rome's experience with this stalwart monotheistic faith, the first it has encountered, differs from the challenge of the Christian faith that emerges from it.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E07 — Christian Challenge - First Conversions
The first years of efforts to convert people to Christianity; the early leadership by James of those who are often called Jewish Christians; the career of Paul, from his own conversion after a vision to his work propagating the message of Jesus.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E08 — Pagan Response - First Persecutions
Early responses to Christianity; the violent persecutions in Rome under Nero; the legalistic and easily avoided persecutions under later emperors; Roman ignorance of Christianity; the eventual momentum that ignorance gives the new faith.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E05 — Origins of Greek Civilization
As the Hittites unite Anatolia, early Greeks called Achaeans visit its western reaches; Achaean warlords trade and raid along the shores of Asia Minor; in time, they become the first Greeks to clash with the armies of a great king to the east.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E06 — The Legend of Troy
The most enduring legacies from early Anatolia are "The Iliad" and "The Odyssey": how the siege of Troy and the exploits of Homer's warrior chieftains fit into the wider tale of imperial struggle and decline during the Greek Dark Age.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E07 — Iron Age Kingdoms of Asia Minor
From 1200 B.C. to 1000 B.C., migrations reshape Anatolia; Phrygians come from the Balkans, only to be overcome by Cimmerian nomads; in the West, Hittite provincials found trade-rich Lydia, whose last king is Croesus.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E08 — Emergence of the Polis
From 750 B.C., the Greeks distinguish themselves with the polis, a city-state based on citizen rule; by 500 B.C., Athens devises the first democratic constitution, with all adult male citizens forming the sovereign assembly.
